`.syzygy/intent/OVERVIEW.md` location. Its narrative identity stays opaque; the
path is a publication location, never authority or an identity. The application
and walkthrough enter that same primary account. Additional named narratives
cannot become a competing default entry.

The entry opens with the project's supported purpose and develops a concise,
coherent argument. Contents, terminology, boundaries and supporting visuals serve
that argument under DESIGN-ACCEPTANCE.md. Review/authority disclosures must remain
clear and accessible without obscuring the reading with a persistent reference
index. Supported limits are explained meaningfully; a generic Refusals heading
is not itself evidence of comprehension.

The fixed entry keeps every applicable narrative obligation: supported and
attributable claims, explicit framing/epistemic state, profile membership,
versioned/attributed/revertible authorship, visible broken or target-changed
anchors, and machine/nonvisual parity. Every exported, embedded or plain-text
form retains presentation-artifact/non-citable metadata. A draft, publication
path or review result is never a source of authoritative project facts.

A known absent entry is a finding; an unobservable entry is Unknown with its
owning reason. Neither produces a fabricated complete manifesto. Publishing or
replacing the entry still needs the existing write, predecessor, authorship and
artifact-specific gates. A fixed destination does not authorize overwrite of
human-owned, digest-bound or otherwise protected bytes. Candidate generation can
continue separately while a conflicting publication target is unresolved.

## Discoverability is a finding, not a README write

For each declared repository of the project, assess at an identified evaluation
whether its root README links to the project entry. No configurable landing file
substitutes for that input. The read must already be admitted; this requirement
grants no new repository-body access. Missing project membership or incomplete
repository coverage stays explicit rather than yielding a complete-looking set.

The finding uses exactly yes, no, not-applicable or Unknown in human and machine
forms. An owner-declined link is no, not an error. A repository without a
governance root carries not-applicable with the declared basis. Unknown carries
its actual RFC2-24 reason and route, including unconsented-source-or-provider for
the upstream unconsented-repository branch and source-uncaptured-or-unreachable
for unavailable input. Not-applicable is this finding's value, not a navigation
outcome or an Unknown reason. A link may be proposed through its governing
Proposal mechanism; Syzygy never writes the root README link.

## Editorial readiness is not an owner verdict

Internal independent source/fidelity/design checks can make a frozen candidate
ready to offer for owner review. They cannot clear a governance review freeze or
record a human verdict on the owner's behalf. Pre-publication checks may use an
explicit candidate preview of the primary account. That preview neither replaces
the published default nor proves a walkthrough of different published bytes; every
formal run names the exact entry/version/context actually traversed. The deterministic materiality floor
covers reading order, section set, canonical diagram set, anchor targets and manifesto/thesis changes;
target-changed anchors trigger review even without prose edits.

For wording-only changes, the author may escalate to material but cannot declare
immaterial. Undeclared wording changes stay open and contestable, not implicitly
immaterial. Owner classification or contest resolution governs de-escalation.
An effective existing failure remains visible while agents prepare repairs;
drafting a repair is not permission to adopt it.

Review-failure judgments live under the governing decisions home, not in the
narrative. A clearing or holding verdict takes effect only through the applicable
owner-act predicate, carrying exact state-(1)/(2) provenance; state-(1) remains
uncorrelated. An ineffective purported pass does not clear the freeze: the failure
stays visible and the prescribed Contradiction is recorded. A stored pass or a
successful generator review cannot manufacture that authority. If no clearing
owner verdict has been submitted, the ordinary state is owner-pending with the
existing failure/freeze visible; an internal pass is not a purported owner verdict
and does not itself mint a Contradiction. A repaired candidate can be ready to
present for owner review while adoption remains frozen.

## Walk the actual page

A fresh reader with no authoring context enters the primary narrative and stays
within Polaris. Their own answers and paths must show:

- why the project exists and what it promises;
- a supported non-goal and its actual rule text;
- major capabilities and how they fit together;
- where exactness lives, reaching a verbatim requirement leaf;
- an honest Unknown and how the page communicates it;
- for a fact the reader chooses, how strongly the page claims to know it and
  what would make that claim stronger.

Then check the answers against the owning admitted sources and record divergences.
A dangling internal link on the walked path or a confident wrong answer caused
by the rendering fails. A reader's misreading of an honest page and a thin
account of an undeclared project remain judgment questions; truthful Unknowns
are not errors to conceal. The independently frozen product-completion oracle
and real-project evaluation requirements remain additional obligations.

Walkthroughs run for material narrative changes and release milestones, with at
least one nonvisual or keyboard-only path traversal per release milestone. The
test exercises movement between units, not screenshots or isolated accessible
controls alone. Performing it grants no release authority.

## Keep records and gates separate

Each walkthrough has a kernel-recorded execution record in the governing records
home, identifying surface version, evaluated context and whether it was nonvisual
or keyboard-only. The owner judgment is a separate decisions-home artifact with
verdict, rationale and judging party, honored only through the effective owner
act and rendered with its exact provenance. Neither record is stored as narrative
or replaced by the generator's Execution Record.

Missing execution evidence leaves the test Unknown-never-met. An unattributed,
unreasoned or ineffectively authorized judgment records verdict-unlawful and also
leaves it Unknown-never-met. That is an invalid judgment, not an invented failed
comprehension test. A valid judgment is never rendered Observed or as a numerical
score, and it remains a warrant rather than project evidence.

For Butlers, the adopted PWB walkthrough evaluator and its record/act-validity
population stay unchanged. Generator quality, answer completeness and readiness
are not new fields or extra arms in that evaluator. A lawful existing judgment
cannot be invalidated by inserting this generator's quality criteria into its
act predicate. Any required amendment must take its own explicit path; new
generator evidence neither replaces that evaluator nor supplies its owner act.

# Generator implementation phases — candidate scope

This is proposed phase applicability for the specification and implementation
package. It is not an owner N/A judgment, an act or permission to implement.
The full owner-facing generator, two real projects and changed-source proof remain
mandatory completion criteria. Finishing an earlier phase cannot close the goal.

## Phase A: reusable mechanics

Implement the source/draft contracts, immutable identities and support, bounded
pure stage controller, dependency invalidation, trusted rendering and fixture
adapters. A thin operator seam exercises the complete data path with explicit
synthetic inputs and effects. It does not create or mutate live scheduler items,
call a real provider, serve owner effect controls, or read another project.
Its previews remain identified test/draft artifacts rather than production or
real-project evidence.

Requirements 001-012, 014-019 and 025 provide the data/reading/failure behavior for
these mechanics. Requirements 013, 020-024 and 026-029 remain integration
obligations; their interfaces are preserved and their implementation/evidence
is not claimed by Phase A. No new normalized-worker projection is introduced in
this phase. Every applicable RFC7 consequence still needs approved mapping or
the required owner-bound N/A before the corresponding observable implementation.

## Phase B: real effects and complete owner flow

Integrate the registered source/provider/lifecycle/artifact adapters, separate
protected host, browser/machine admission, durable audit, work materialization,
start/progress/cancel/resume/review/repair and the fixed project reading entry.
Use the same core from Phase A. The CLI remains a diagnostic/operator interface;
manual record assembly cannot replace the owner flow.

Generation-stage panels carry typed stage/receipt facts and an explicit link to
the owning drafting work item. They are not a replacement for its lifecycle.
The following consumers project work state and therefore must retain requirement
028's qualified raw, normalized and chain fields: the drafting-work drawer,
Trajectory work rows, work filters/counts, work exports and machine work answers.
Narrative prose, diagram nodes, glossary and stage receipts do not become work
items merely because work produced them.

The generator does not manufacture or infer a worker-liveness bound from model
timeout, run deadline or receipt cadence. An admitted execution profile with no
effective worker bound uses the existing activity-undetermined predicate; its
actual missing-bound state remains visible. No profile may silently discard or
replace an effective bound to reach that case.

If a selected profile/consumer requires a work-state case for which the accepted
mapping has no predicate, that projection is unsupported and the affected live
run is not admitted until its required mapping/act is effective. A different
profile is an explicit owner choice, not automatic fallback. In particular,
claimed work with an effective bound and no qualifying VCS/PR signal cannot be
reported active, assigned an invented absence value, or treated as fully
conformant merely because provider receipts exist. Any required predicate
amendment is resolved at this integration boundary, not by changing source or
asset validation. This is a refusal boundary, not proof that the unsupported
case has been implemented.

## Phase C: real quality, portability and regeneration

Complete the final real-project proof using the identical engine, prompts,
validators, renderer and supported execution profile. Project source identities,
audience/profile content and separately effective permissions may differ.
Mechanical fixtures, a CLI-only run or unknown mandatory owner-flow behavior
cannot satisfy this phase.

Use independently admitted real revisions to exercise a meaning change. Existing
historical and later revisions may be suitable; the proof must actually revise
the prior bundle from changed source, not merely display two unrelated pages.
Do not edit an observed project just to construct a test without write consent.
Frozen reader questions, independent whole-source fidelity, actual full-page
visual/keyboard review and repair confirmation remain required.

## Approval and phase claims

The owner package must name the phase scope it authorizes. Source/provider/write
permissions are still evaluated at their effect seams. A phase-specific approval
is not approval to bypass later requirements. A whole-generator completion claim
requires all three phases and every applicable requirement to be satisfied.
Unresolved normalized-worker support is reported specifically; it is neither a
reason to call Phase A complete before it works nor a reason to claim the full
owner workflow complete while a required work projection is unsupported.

# Candidate generator interfaces and ownership

Proposed interface decisions for review. This is not an accepted schema or an
adapter registration. The specification owns observable behavior; existing
identity, act, source-state and namespace contracts remain controlling.

## Boundary model

The generator has no filesystem crawler, shell tool or implicit network route.
Acquisition supplies an identified bundle; an admission service resolves its
permissions independently; a provider adapter dispatches bounded content; the
lifecycle adapter records execution; the artifact adapter performs separately
consented writes. Model output can request missing information as a finding, but
cannot invoke any of these interfaces or supply permission state.

SCHEMA-CONTRACT.md defines record ownership, requested/produced variants, identity
issuance, typed anchors, reference integrity and version behavior.

SOURCE-POLICY.md specifies consent granularity, provenance-derived classification,
every-ingest screening and the distinct whole-artifact/partial-redaction outcomes.

The proposed versioned interchange is structured data with explicit variants.
Unknown variants/versions and extra effect-bearing fields are refused. Content
and diagnostic byte limits apply before parsing or persistence.

| Record | Required content | Validation and authority boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Source bundle | Schema version; opaque project, snapshot and evaluation references; presentation-profile reference/state; admitted source references and content digests; captured declaration/observation/execution claims and their original epistemic tuples; exclusions | All references resolve within the admitted snapshot. The bundle's own approval claims confer no permission. A changed referenced object invalidates the bundle |
| Source inventory | Source-bundle identity; independent preparer/provenance; complete admitted-source denominator; material claims, qualifications, conflicts, trade-offs and explicit relevance/omission dispositions | Prepared or validated inside the bounded run, then frozen before candidate narrative drafting. Prepared from sources and governing questions, without the generator's draft/outline as its denominator |
| Generation request | Stable request identity; project/snapshot; source-inventory preparation policy and optional reusable inventory reference; profile/audience context; generation-policy identity; permitted provider route reference; explicit budget; requested asset kinds | A trusted admission evaluation resolves permissions immediately before each effect. Reusing a request identity with different inputs is a conflict, not an update |
| Stage artifact | Run/stage/attempt identities; parent inputs and digests; producing adapter/model/policy versions; screened output reference/digest; actual usage receipt or explicit unavailable/uncertain usage with reason; result kind | A file or HTTP success does not imply validity. Outputs are validated and screened before durable content storage or rendering. Invalid bodies are not exposed in logs |
| Asset bundle | Opaque bundle identity/version; project/snapshot/profile; editorial state; Narrative/Sections/blocks/reading order; source anchors with captured states; typed presentation assets and per-requested-asset dispositions; generation provenance; review bindings | Uses RFC7's roles and closed anchor classes. Claims and framing remain distinct. Links are references resolved by trusted rendering, never arbitrary model-supplied URLs |
| Review record | Exact bundle and source-inventory identities/digests; independent review provenance; reviewed population; findings, severity and dispositions; exact verdict and applicability | Source-to-draft and draft-to-source coverage are both checked. Changed subjects retire the applicable verdict. A review is not an owner act |
| Authorship request | Exact eligible bundle/blocks; per-block attestations; expected predecessor; effective owner-act reference | Evaluates RFC3-16/RFC7-21 rather than trusting a human flag. Writes require their own effective consent and atomic predecessor check |

ASSET-CONTRACT.md defines the proposed closed asset kinds, their record content,
reviewable omissions and curated/computed boundary. A computed reference retains
its owning renderer's obligations; it is not an arbitrary embed or permission to
activate deferred live transclusion. Required unsupported assets stay unresolved.

Generation provenance distinguishes requested model identity from provider-reported
identity/version. An unavailable provider revision is explicitly unreported, never
filled from an assumption about an alias. The declared reproducibility standard
is recipe replay from retained permitted inputs; generated bytes are not promised
identical. A policy requiring a reproducibility guarantee the provider cannot
supply refuses that route explicitly.

These records do not mint new global epistemic values. Run progress, profile
state, editorial-draft/curated state and underlying source claims are separately
queryable. The source inventory is review evidence, not adopted project intent.

SECURITY-CONTRACT.md defines caller admission, per-operation authorization,
protected audit and immediate revocation behavior. A successful scheduler
observation or local commitment never replaces these effect-boundary checks.

NAVIGATION-CONTRACT.md defines shared selection, scenario, drawer and query
semantics, including complete aggregate composition and principal-before-query
admission. Presentation hints and disclosure depth never create another fact set.

WORK-STATE-CONTRACT.md separates recorded generation progress from normalized
work/chain state and defines capture/chain obligations. Its identified missing-
signal derivation case remains an explicit conformance decision, not a fallback.

## Effect interfaces

- **Admission:** Given project, source snapshot, provider/content class or write
  destination and evaluation instant, return the existing permission evaluation
  with its exact provenance and refusal reasons. The generator cannot supply an
  override. Acquisition integrity is checked against the owning records: changing
  claim text while retaining a legitimate source reference is not a valid bundle. Re-evaluation occurs before dispatch, resume, adoption and export.
- **Provider:** Accept a reserved attempt identity, admitted content and hard
  request/output bounds. Return screened-candidate input plus usage/dispatch
  receipts. Tool/function requests in output are not executed. A provider without
  a usable bound or permission cannot be selected silently as a fallback.
- **Lifecycle:** Scheduler mutations use the scheduler's typed adapter,
  synchronously and attributed, followed by a re-read. Separately, conditional
  execution-control writes compare an execution-control revision and append one
  identified run/attempt event. An already-applied event is returned as such;
  a changed revision is a conflict. Scheduler revisions and control revisions
  are distinct fields. No independent generator queue exists under intent or
  in a private task database.
- **Artifact:** Read/write an identified projection or authored artifact through
  its proper home and consent. Authored changes use expected-predecessor comparison,
  atomic replacement and attributed reversal; they never overwrite unfamiliar
  authored bytes as a cache refresh.

ADAPTER-DECLARATIONS.md specifies the adapter registration fields, ownership,
failure mapping and complete run envelope that stage artifacts do not replace.
The corresponding registry entries and schema placement still require their
applicable review and effective acts before operational admission. These
interfaces select separation of responsibilities, not a storage engine or SDK.

OWNER-FLOW.md defines request preparation, exact work reuse, missing-approval
handling and materialization before this dispatch protocol. A caller is not
required to assemble the work records manually.

## Budget and retry decisions

Each run supplies positive finite `maxCalls`, `maxInputBytes`, `maxOutputBytes`,
`maxUsageUnits` and `maxElapsedMs`, plus finite nonnegative `maxRepairCycles`,
with a versioned accounting
unit/policy reference. There is no implicit unlimited value or agent-selected
spending default. The UI can prefill an effective owner-approved preset and
show its bounds before start; ordinary runs do not require re-entering technical
limits or re-granting still-effective consent. The policy maps provider limits to worst-case reservations;
unbounded or unknown required accounting refuses that provider dispatch.

The original start and absolute deadline are durable. Downtime consumes elapsed
budget and resume cannot extend the deadline. Reservations and actual receipts
are distinct; a missing final receipt is uncertain usage, not zero. Late receipts
are attached to their original attempt even after cancellation. A new retry
decision must identify the uncertain prior attempt and explicitly reserve its
maximum additional cost; it never rewrites the earlier uncertainty as absence.

Execution event proposals include request identity, attempt identity, expected
execution-control revision, separately identified scheduler observation/revision,
and artifact digests. The adapter's conditional write determines
which competing event applies. Accepted cancellation/rejection before authored-write commitment prevents a
later stage-success event from making a draft ready. Late requests after that
commitment are reported as too late, not falsely acknowledged as cancellation. A failed conditional update is
reported and reconciled from the authoritative work record, not retried blindly.

## Durable dispatch reservation

The registered lifecycle adapter is the sole writer of run-budget reservations
and dispatch claims in their declared execution-control record. This is not
ownership of scheduler lifecycle: after materialization scheduler fields are
read from the scheduler at the answering evaluation and are never mirrored as
editable generator fields. Both surfaces are projections of those owning records.
Execution-control schemas must identify their field ownership explicitly before
registration; they cannot redefine scheduler state or the immutable materialization
join. They are subordinate metadata of the existing Execution run and Execution
Record identities (RFC8-4), not new kernel entities. A reservation requires the
valid immutable materialization join and applicable warranted execution authority;
an orphan finding blocks dispatch pending owner adjudication. Before a provider
call, the execution-control transaction atomically compares its own control
revision, request/stage identity, cancellation/rejection state, original deadline
and remaining budget, then records one reserved attempt and its maximum charge.
Only a successful durable reservation can proceed. Competing callers cannot both
reserve the same stage or spend the same allowance; losers receive the existing
attempt or an explicit conflict without contacting the provider.

A reserved attempt becomes dispatching through a second conditional transition
that grants exactly one dispatcher the attempt. Fresh admission is checked at the
effect boundary; failure before dispatch records a known refusal. No network call
is legal before the dispatching transition is durable. A crash after that point
is conservatively uncertain even if it happened just before the network call.
Lease expiry is not permission to send the attempt again.

An uncertain reservation continues to consume its reserved availability until a
trusted receipt or effect-and-usage resolution establishes the actual effect and usage. Recovery
never infers no effect from a missing response or missing file. A known unsent
reservation can be released through the lifecycle adapter; an uncertain effect
requires authoritative effect-and-usage resolution or an explicit new bounded retry attempt.
The new attempt references the old uncertainty and cannot silently reuse its
allowance. No automatic new run resets budgets to evade the original bound.

### Dispatch admission and scheduler observation

A dispatch admission is the durable transition from reserved to dispatching. It
is the ordering point for accepted local cancellation and exclusive ownership,
not proof that a provider received bytes. From that point the attempt is
potentially in flight, including the crash window before the network call.
Reservation alone is not admission. A cancellation that wins before admission
prevents it; one that follows admission prevents later admissions and attempts
supported cancellation of the admitted effect without claiming it stopped.

For every admission, including a retry or resumed reservation:

1. Read the scheduler through its registered adapter in a new admission
   evaluation. Bind the work-item identity, scheduler revision, capture instant
   and evaluation to an immutable observation reference. Validate the existing
   materialization join and execution warrant at that evaluation. Missing,
   withdrawn, superseded, ineligible or unavailable required scheduler state
   refuses admission; a last-good permissive projection cannot authorize it.
2. Evaluate the applicable consent and effect permissions through their own
   authority service. A scheduler observation never stands in for provider or
   content consent. Recheck these permissions at the provider effect boundary.
3. In the execution-control transaction, compare the expected control revision,
   original deadline, remaining allowance and accepted cancellation/rejection
   disposition. Verify the observation is still within the declared admission
   freshness bound; a future-dated or expired observation is refused. Bind it
   to this attempt and atomically grant one dispatcher exclusive ownership.
4. Initiate the single bounded provider attempt through the provider adapter.
   A known refusal before sending is recorded without a provider charge; lack
   of proof that nothing was sent remains an uncertain reserved effect. Neither
   expiry of dispatch ownership nor process recovery grants permission to send
   the same admitted attempt again.

The transaction is atomic over execution control only. Scheduler state may
change after capture, even before physical transmission. The record means
eligible at the named admission evaluation, never guaranteed unchanged through
provider completion. It stores historical evidence, not an editable copy of
current scheduler state. No scheduler mutation is required just to observe
eligibility; offered mutations still use its attributed adapter and re-read.

Every later stage admission and each transition to ready or authored-write
commitment re-observes the scheduler under the same eligibility/freshness check.
When withdrawal or
supersession is subsequently observed, the control service blocks further
admissions, readiness and not-yet-committed finalization, attempts supported cancellation of
admitted operations, and records outcomes and late usage without changing the
materialization join. An authored-write commitment already made retains its
existing ordering semantics; a subsequent request cannot falsely claim reversal.
An admitted operation may have completed; report that
fact rather than rewriting it as cancelled. Resume cannot use a previous
permissive observation or an old local plan to bypass this check.

This selects an observation-based scheduler guarantee under RFC4-5/15 and
RFC8-7/9/10. It does not weaken consent-revocation enforcement or promise
instantaneous detection of external scheduler changes. Adapter declarations
must expose the observation/freshness behavior, source failures and provider
cancellation support; implementation tests exercise the boundary directly.

## Authored-write commitment and receipt recovery

The lifecycle adapter also serializes cancellation/rejection against finalization.
After valid per-block owner-act evaluation, current write admission, exact bundle
review checks and predecessor identification, one conditional operation records
an authored-write commitment. It references the governing owner act, immutable
bundle, destination, expected predecessor and a unique finalization identity;
it contains no narrative body and is not a second copy of the owner act.

This commitment is the ordering boundary. If accepted cancellation/rejection
wins first, commitment is refused and no authored write is dispatched. If the
commitment wins first, a later cancellation/rejection request reports too late
and the current finalization state; it must not claim the run was cancelled or
the artifact undone. Reversal is a separate consented, attributed action.
Commitment is not evidence that the artifact has been written or adopted on the
surface: that state waits for verified application of the authorized write.

The artifact adapter consumes the unique finalization identity idempotently,
rechecks applicable write permission at the effect boundary, and atomically
records the resulting artifact/version and application receipt together. The
receipt binds finalization identity, owner-act reference, exact written digest
and predecessor. It is durable in the owning artifact's version/receipt home,
not in a competing work queue. A consent failure or conflicting predecessor is
an explicit refused finalization; commitment cannot override those gates.

If the write succeeds but its work acknowledgment is lost, recovery reads that
receipt and reconciles the work projection without another write or act. If the
artifact was subsequently edited by a human, recovery reports the applied
version and the newer state; it cannot restore the old bytes over the new edit.
Absent or expired receipts do not prove non-application: unresolved finalization
remains uncertain and requires receipt recovery or authoritative effect resolution. Receipt retention must cover the
policy's recovery horizon; after that horizon automated replay is unavailable.

## Retention decisions

Generation requires an effective project retention policy naming bounded expiry
for draft projections and expirable raw execution detail, permitted storage homes
and deletion behavior. Missing policy refuses durable generation. Policy inputs
cannot remove RFC8-26's preservation set or override another artifact's governing
retention obligations.

- Expired or rejected drafts cease to appear in Polaris reading, search and
  adoption surfaces. Rejection is recorded on the authoritative work item;
  retained history is not adoptable prose.
- Rejected or unclassifiable provider output is never retained as diagnostic
  prose. Record only permitted error kind, identity/digest and bounded metadata.
- Structured run summaries, work warrants, decisions, materialization mappings,
  known cost/token totals, evidence identities and hashes, and reconciliation
  outcomes survive every compaction in their owning homes. Cleanup does not
  delete this preservation set or convert missing usage into zero.
- Raw transcripts and verbose logs may expire under declared policy. Each
  compaction is an identified, durable record; retention events identify affected
  artifacts so dependent claims can cite the event. Independently governed review
  artifacts keep their preservation obligations and historical bindings.
- A claim whose only substantiation expired renders Unknown citing the retention
  event, never absence or a confident reconstruction from its summary. Preserved
  summaries retain their recorded tiers. Missing artifacts render broken references
  and affect tier in the next identified evaluation; display queries never rewrite
  immutable evaluation conclusions or upgrade tiers.
- Provider expiry does not erase retained confirmation captures. Later authorized
  re-confirmation produces a new observation. A preserved hash without the required
  capture or another satisfied RFC4-13 route caps at report-fact, visibly; it cannot
  establish gate-backed evidence. No records found remains visually and queryably
  distinct from nothing happened.
- Authored composition lives in the intent home, is versioned and individually
  revertible, and survives offboarding. Projection cleanup never deletes it.
- Export needs separate destination/content authorization and preserves draft or
  authored state. Neither retention nor recovery authorizes additional source
  reads, provider calls or remote publication.

ENTRY-AND-WALKTHROUGH.md specifies the fixed primary publication entry,
read-only repository discoverability finding, review-freeze authority and the
separate walkthrough execution/judgment records.

## Review protocol

Within the bounded run, an independent preparation stage creates or validates
the source inventory and project-specific reader questions from the admitted
snapshot. It runs in a separate request context that receives sources and
governing questions, not candidate prose, drafting instructions or the authoring
conversation. Producing an inventory and draft in one response does not establish
this independence. Its provider
calls and review consume the same declared run budget. The owner is not required
to hand-author an inventory, expected answers or a project-specific outline before
starting. These artifacts are frozen before candidate narrative drafting. The opening must explain the supported purpose and thesis; the concise
account must explain motives, promises and refusals; deeper reading must explain
capability relationships and reach exact intent. Review each stopping depth before
using deeper material to answer its questions.

The fidelity reviewer receives the owning admitted sources as well as the
inventory and candidate. It checks inventory accuracy/completeness against those
sources before using it for coverage. The fidelity record covers every material
inventory entry and every generated claim-bearing block. It identifies explicit justified omissions, unsupported
claims and misplaced/unused anchors. Labelling unsupported speculation Inferred
cannot make it eligible. The rendered review records desktop/mobile and keyboard
experience, including source/path walls, dead or hidden destinations and reference
material that overwhelms the argument.

Confident source-induced factual errors, inability to explain a supported central
thesis or capability relationships, unresolved material omissions, inaccessible
required paths and blocking visual findings prevent completion. Record failures
and their repairs; a changed artifact requires a fresh applicable evaluation.
Two independently admitted real project domains and real source-change
regeneration are required. At least one case must need synthesis across verbose
or scattered sources, so a polished input document cannot stand in for the engine.

## External completion evidence

The run's internal preparation and reviews are product behavior, not the test
oracle for declaring the generator complete. Independent product evaluators
freeze their questions and expected source-backed answers outside the generator
under test before candidate drafting. They do not derive their denominator or
expected verdict from its inventory, outline or review output. This evaluation
work is distinct from the ordinary owner start flow and does not require owners
to prepare a dossier for every generation request.

# Manifesto navigation and shared answers — candidate

Proposed detail for REQ-polaris-generation-026/027. This defines the generator's
integration with the shared selection/query contract, not a second fact store,
new client permission or authority to fetch additional content.

## Explore without losing the question

From a capability, claim, diagram element or work reference, the reader can open
Why this answer?, follow its supporting records, and continue in the appropriate
surface. The selection keeps its project, durable identity, evaluation and
scenario. Returning to the narrative may restore personal reading position or
density; those presentation hints never change the resolved facts.

The host first admits the principal and authorizes project/operation access.
Only then does selection resolution apply. An unauthorized principal receives no
project counts or metadata disguised as an unconsented navigation result. Query
filters select authorized scope; they cannot grant access. Project/provider
consent remains the separate policy predicate inside authorized resolution.

## Durable selections and time

A selection names an existing kernel or project-loaded profile entity by its
owning kind and durable identity, optionally evaluation-qualified, with one
scenario context. Paths, labels, scene indices and coordinates are not identity.
Private renderer handles resolve to this reference before crossing a URL,
surface or endpoint. A presentation-profile selection is still not a valid
source-anchor target merely because it is selectable.

Unqualified evaluation means the latest identified evaluation available at
resolution, named in the answer. A pinned selection keeps its historical answer
and exposes supersession/staleness; it cannot silently move to newer source
bytes. A rename or layout change does not break the identity-based URL. Retired
identities show retirement and successor choices, never automatic redirection.
Changing or stripping a preferred-surface/view hint preserves the same selection
and answer. The same selection is openable across surfaces; lack of a surface
projection is handled explicitly rather than losing the selection.

Scenario is exactly one of the existing Base, Proposed or Historical contexts.
Base is the default; a non-default-revision Base view names that revision.
Proposed carries its base evaluation and mutually compatible selected proposal
set. Exclusive or undeclared-compatible proposals produce incompatible-scenario
and separate candidate futures, never a merged plan or aggregate. Proposed
structure stays distinct and confers no status authority. Historical names a
superseded immutable evaluation and shows staleness. Every URL, handoff and query
carries the context; a surface cannot silently substitute another.

## Total resolution, with policy first

The kernel returns the first applicable outcome in the existing precedence:
excluded, unconsented, incompatible-scenario, unresolvable, retired,
resolved-absent, unknown, resolved. No private spelling, empty panel, unexplained
error or dropped selection replaces an outcome. Not-applicable belongs only to a
surface with no projection; it does not replace the kernel outcome and is never
a kernel, URL or endpoint result. That surface still offers the shared facts and
names the surfaces where the selection projects.

Each outcome keeps its governing detail: excluded carries count; unconsented is
the standing policy state with its consent route; incompatible-scenario names the
conflict; unresolvable names the failed reference and treats a kernel-emitted
dangling link as a trust-floor incident; retired offers successors;
resolved-absent names evaluations where the identity is present; unknown carries
each governing claim's primary reason/route and separate secondary annotations;
resolved offers the complete fact set. Navigation outcomes never become claim
Unknown reasons or enter their counts.

## One Why this answer? fact set

At one selection/evaluation/scenario, all surfaces and machine answers use the
same kernel-computed fact set. Different grouping and density are allowed;
different facts, labels or provenance are not. If a consumer can answer only at
another evaluation, it names both identities and exposes the skew rather than
mixing them. Minimal display hides detail without deleting it, and machine
queries serve the complete authorized fact set. This does not mean embedding
every source body: resolvable evidence links and metadata preserve their roles,
while verbatim text remains on its separately admitted owning route.

The fact set keeps all eight RFC6-19 groups where applicable:

| Group | Required content |
|---|---|
| Identity | Owning kind and durable identity, labels, lifecycle/succession and the governing state plane of each fact |
| Epistemic state | Governing claims' verbatim label, tier, primary/secondary reasons and freshness; suspended basis remains visible |
| Evidence | Every supporting artifact's resolvable reference, source, capture time, scope, integrity and visible revision binding |
| Provenance | Evaluation, typed answering authority, governing normative revision and observer/adapter versions |
| Warrant | Governing/motivating decisions, requirements and policies, including dismissal reason/expiry without a positive-state upgrade |
| Challenges and contradictions | Every open challenge with lifecycle and inference provenance, including submitted challenge-pending separately from admitted suspension, and pending adjudications |
| Policy | Consent, counted exclusions and the actual coverage boundary: executed mapping records plus explicitly captured scope of a partial snapshot |
| Work and reconciliation | Separate chain and normalized-work fields where work bears on the selection; uncomputed reconciliation is Unknown, never inferred from work completion |

Labels, tiers, freshness and reasons are copied from the owning evaluated state,
not synthesized by the narrative. Sibling dismissed-by-decision, unadopted-draft
and editorial-draft states remain distinct; challenge-pending travels beside the
claim tuple and does not suspend it. Internal links resolve to their identified
targets. External links remain classified external, with different availability
semantics; neither link class authorizes a body read on its own.

## Filters, aggregates and parity

Every answer names its evaluation and declared filters/scope. A partial or
filtered answer never claims whole-project coverage. Deterministic answers agree
for the same evaluation, scope and scenario. A finer textual view than a visual
aggregate is valid when its filter/aggregation difference is disclosed.

An aggregate has no label, tier, Unknown reason or freshness of its own. It gives
its membership count and expandable member composition: per-label, all six
tiers, primary Unknown reasons, freshness, sibling states, pending challenges and
applicable chain/normalized-work values. Secondary Unknown annotations are
separate and never inflate primary-reason totals. Work-state and navigation
absence values do not enter the claim-reason counts.

Equivalent renderings preserve the full evaluation/filter/graph/epistemic/sibling/
challenge/work/chain/scenario tuple. Counts over the same scope must agree.
Layout may differ, semantics may not; a disagreement is a projection/kernel
defect and cannot pass the release check. Every required selection, disclosure
and handoff remains keyboard/nonvisual operable under the presentation contract,
including the route back to the reading, not just the individual controls.

# Requesting a manifesto — candidate flow

Proposed owner experience for REQ-polaris-generation-020. This describes the
future application, not authority to perform any of these operations now.

## Open the project and choose the outcome

The owner opens Polaris and chooses to generate or refresh the project's
manifesto. The application resolves the selected project's declared governance
root and authorized work/artifact homes; it does not infer writable locations
from the observed source repository. Missing or conflicting declarations remain
explicit setup failures, with the available honest project view still readable.

The request uses known project context and an effective preset where available.
The owner sees the purpose of the run, source scope, provider, spending/time
bounds and requested assets in ordinary language. Technical identifiers and
supporting records are reachable in detail; the start screen does not require
copying paths, writing manifests, finding scheduler identifiers or re-entering
still-effective consent. Unknown prerequisites are named rather than defaulted.

The start flow needs no model call to prepare its own authorization. Initial
preparation uses admitted metadata, the owner's requested outcome and the
existing policies/requirements. It neither reads additional project bodies nor
sends data to a provider to discover whether sending data is permitted. Draft
effect plans can be shown transiently before write permission; persisting a
proposal or request record requires its own effective write authority.

## Resolve warranted work

The application checks for an existing, explicitly reusable work binding covering
this project, requested purpose, pinned warranted intent revision and effect
scope. It validates its immutable materialization record, current scheduler
eligibility, remaining authorized allowance and applicable approvals. A matching title or old successful run is
not a match. If several candidates remain and the effective policy does not
select one unambiguously, show the meaningful choices; do not choose the newest
record or merge incompatible proposals. A new regeneration cannot reuse an
exhausted or narrower authorization or rewrite an existing pinned warrant.

When no reusable binding exists, the application prepares the execution-intent
Proposal and effect plan for the owner. The plan makes requested source/provider,
storage, scheduler and budget effects concrete. It records what existing authority
covers and which approvals are missing. Preparation is not approval. A prior
Decision may cover the exact new work only when its recorded scope says so;
child proposals inherit approval only when the parent's Decision explicitly
permits it. No standing approval is invented to make the flow shorter.

The owner completes any genuinely missing approval through its existing gate.
The application supplies the records and context; the owner does not assemble
governance files or scheduler commands. A generic Generate action is not silently
interpreted as a missing specification, policy, provider-consent or execution
approval. Once required authority is effective, the same request continues from
its recorded state without asking again for unchanged approvals.

## Materialize once, then execute

The approved execution-intent Proposal keeps its identity. A recorded
queued-for-materialization fact is not a new kernel state and is not labelled
scheduled. The application uses the project's registered scheduler adapter for
the authorized creation/reuse operation. The durable materialization record
binds proposal identity, scheduler-issued work-item identity set and the exact
warranted intent revision; the materializing evaluation is retained alongside.

The written record is the transition boundary. Before it exists, the Proposal
remains authoritative for planned work. After it exists, the scheduler owns work
lifecycle and the Proposal is terminal materialized. Only then may the existing
dispatch-admission protocol evaluate and reserve a provider attempt. No stage
skips the record because scheduler creation returned success.

If scheduler creation succeeded but recording failed, show the orphaned-work
Contradiction and keep its affected conclusion Unknown. Never silently create a
replacement, fill in the missing record, delete the orphan or send a provider
request. Recovery follows owner adjudication; an authorized re-materialization
cites and supersedes the finding. Duplicate start/request identities return the
same preparation, Proposal and materialization outcome or an explicit conflict,
never independent scheduler creations. Creation has a stable operation identity
and exclusive durable claim before the scheduler call; duplicate callers cannot
both create. Supported idempotency or authoritative lookup may establish an
existing result, but no such substrate capability is presumed. An uncertain scheduler effect is retained
as uncertain and is not automatically retried. If enumeration observes an item
without its record, calling it materialization in progress cannot hide the
required orphan finding. Ordinary editorial stages remain subordinate run
metadata; they do not require a child Proposal or work item for every model call.

## Follow the draft through review

The owner sees preparation, missing approval, queued-for-materialization,
generation stage, review, repair and ready-for-owner as their correctly qualified
states. These stages do not become normalized scheduler or intent-reconciliation
states. Progress and recoverable errors are visible; returning to the project
restores the identified request and its actual next step.

Cancellation before dispatch admission prevents new provider effects under the
existing ordering rule. It does not erase already prepared or materialized work:
scheduler lifecycle changes use the scheduler adapter and their own authority,
while historical records remain. During execution, late effects, usage and
partial results follow the existing cancellation/recovery contract.

Successful generation produces a reviewed editorial candidate. The owner can
read it as a coherent manifesto, inspect meaningful changes and sources, and
perform applicable per-block authorship acts. An unsigned profile, failed review
or unresolved required asset remains explicit. A completed work item, model
response or generic start action never adopts the narrative or establishes
product comprehension. Regeneration preserves the previous authored version
until the authorized replacement is actually applied.

# Generator interchange — candidate schema contract

Proposed representation for review, before executable schemas and registration.
This is not an installed plane schema, migration or implementation. It refines
INTERFACES.md and ASSET-CONTRACT.md without replacing kernel identities, source
state vocabularies or effective owner-act evaluation.

## One owning record for each kind of information

| Record | Owns | References, never replaces |
|---|---|---|
| Generation request | Request identity, requested assets, audience/profile input, budget and selected route | Project/snapshot, effective permissions, policy and existing work binding |
| Source inventory | Independently prepared review denominator and omission dispositions | Owning source identities, declarations and captured evidence |
| Run controls | Local reservation, dispatch-admission and finalization ordering facts | Scheduler observations, execution authority and immutable Execution Records |
| Asset bundle | Editorial composition and generated content | Source anchors, existing claim tuples, source inventory and review bindings |
| Execution Record | Historical execution envelope | Source receipts, run/work identities and their declared joins |
| Authored artifact | Adopted presentation and its attributed version | Effective per-block act, reviewed candidate and predecessor/application receipt |

All records carry their declared class/version and project identity. Version
selection is explicit; missing versions are invalid. Record digests bind canonical
bytes after validation, never stand in for adoption, and never include mutable
render-time presentation state. Exact canonicalization rules and executable
encodings are implementation artifacts reviewed against this contract, not an
opportunity to change identifier semantics.

## Requested assets and output assets are different records

A requested asset has a stable request-local identity, requested kind, role,
requiredness and the source of that requirement (request, reading obligation or
frozen acceptance criterion). It has no fabricated output identity or digest.
Requiredness cannot be downgraded by provider output.

Each request resolves to exactly one disposition:

| Disposition | Required payload | Invariant |
|---|---|---|
| Produced | References to one or more validated output assets | Every reference resolves in the same bundle; produced does not mean reviewed, adopted or acceptable |
| Omitted | Reviewable reason and supporting disposition reference | Only optional assets whose omission preserves every reading obligation; not a substitute for unavailable capability |
| Unresolved | Missing support, permission, capability or failed-validation reason, with the relevant references | No output digest or asset is invented; the affected readiness obligation stays unmet |

A produced asset may satisfy several requests when the relationship is explicit.
Multiple placements may reuse one asset without cloning its identity. Every
produced asset also records why it exists in the reading structure, including
assets chosen by the generator that were not individually requested by the owner.
Unresolved requests remain visible separately from the valid produced population.

The six produced kinds are the ASSET-CONTRACT.md roles. Their common envelope
contains asset identity, class/version, project and bundle identity, editorial
state, input/generation provenance and review references. Type-specific fields
are required only for that produced kind; unresolved computed references do not
pretend to contain a successful renderer digest or text equivalent.

## Content structure and identities

The bundle stores unique definitions for sections, claim blocks, supporting
assets, glossary entries and source anchors, with explicit typed references
between them. Identical labels never merge objects. Repeated rendered occurrences
retain the owning object identity; occurrence count is not distinct-claim count.
Distinct summaries offered simultaneously are separate blocks with their own
support and review bindings. Editing an existing unit follows its governing
identity/version discipline; it never changes the bytes or meaning of a
historical revision silently.

Provider-local handles are temporary references, never minted presentation or
kernel identities. The trusted recorded authoring operation issues opaque
presentation identities under RFC7-5 and retains the local-to-issued mapping in
its provenance. Generating a draft is recorded as draft production, not a human
authorship/adoption act. Existing identities can be referenced only through
validated owning records; neither a provider-supplied UUID nor an existing label
permits reuse or replacement. Effective editorial/profile/adoption state is
evaluated separately from serialized producer assertions. An unsigned profile
keeps every narrative element visibly unadopted even when generation succeeded.


The narrative roles remain anchored-project-fact, non-normative-framing and
epistemic-claim. Support references are confined to claims within their owning
block and must make each claim's actual support recoverable; an ambiguous block
must be split, not excused because every anchor resolves.

Canonical anchors use RFC7-10's target-specific variants:

| Variant | Identity and state required |
|---|---|
| Kernel entity | Owning RFC6 selection reference and optional fragment; captured evaluation identity plus verbatim label, tier and reason at authoring |
| Doctrine or accepted-contract citation | Stable owning rule/clause identifier, optional fragment and captured artifact revision |
| OpenSpec anchor | Artifact-contract identity/anchor, optional fragment and captured artifact revision |
| Decision or policy | Owning identifier, optional fragment and captured artifact revision |
| Evidence artifact | Owning evidence identifier, integrity digest, optional fragment and captured artifact revision |

No variant targets narrative, rendering or editorial draft. Captured state is
observed at the recorded authoring operation and never rewritten on later reads.
Missing/broken source resolution follows the governing primary-surface and
machine Unknown/reason/route behavior; no guessed rebinding or automatic successor
redirect makes an old anchor valid. Locators remain descriptive, not identities.

The existing PWB wire form has six local classes (doctrine, contract, requirement,
decision, evidence and work) and a universal revision field. Preserve that adopted
surface through an explicit compatibility adapter; do not promote that TypeScript
shape into the generic wire schema or assume a revision is an evaluation identity.
The adapter resolves each target through its owning typed route and preserves
its exact meaning. If the required canonical identity/state cannot be recovered,
report the typed inability to adapt rather than inventing it. PWB-specific
unstated/none conventions are not new global epistemic values. No generic policy
or kernel variant widens Butlers' adopted source/anchor admission.

Content is an inert tree of paragraphs, text spans, emphasis, inline code, lists
and trusted references. Tables use explicit headers and cell blocks; glossary
links name glossary entries; contents name real sections. Provider content cannot
supply raw HTML, script, styles, event handlers, external requests or arbitrary
embed URLs. Exact normative leaves use the existing verbatim route and owning
text, never the generated prose tree as a replacement source.

Section/asset containment and stage-input dependency graphs are acyclic; required
internal references resolve. Glossary cross-references may cycle. This does not
forbid cycles in a project's actual relationship graph:
diagram edges can represent supported cycles. Diagram nodes and edges reference
defined elements and carry support/markings, legend and equivalent structured
text. Neither a missing node nor an unsupported edge is repaired by inventing a
fact. Reference validation checks both directions: no dangling references and no
unused anchors or accidentally orphaned required content.

## Parse, resolve and judge separately

1. Bound bytes before parsing, then reject duplicate object keys, unknown
   versions/kinds, duplicate definitions and undeclared effect-bearing fields.
   Finite numeric budgets and structural bounds are validated before effects;
   null, missing or a numeric sentinel never means unlimited.
2. Validate the variant's required fields and internal structure. An unavailable
   expected execution-envelope value has the prescribed Unknown representation
   and reason; it is not an invalid record merely because it is unavailable.
3. Resolve identities, revisions, source roles, captured states, permissions and
   profile/registry acts against owning records. Pure shape validation grants no
   authority and cannot establish source fidelity.
4. Apply the independent inventory/fidelity and rendered-design review. Produced
   and structurally valid remain separate from ready, authored and accepted.

Validation failure retains only permitted bounded diagnostics and the unresolved
asset/run disposition. It cannot silently drop an offending field or array tail
and call the original output complete. Last-good authored presentation remains
governed by its own source/drift state, not overwritten by malformed generation.

## Version and migration behavior

Per-class versions are snapshot inputs under RFC3-22. An unsupported newer plane
is never written or downgraded; uninterpretable content renders Unknown rather
than a partially understood whole. Older supported content is read through its
declared interpretation/migration path without mutation on read. A persisted
migration requires its own reviewed, attributed, atomic and reversible act.
Migrations preserve minted identities, adoption state, attribution, timestamps,
consent scope, dismissal reasons/expiry, evidence digests and citation resolution.
A change to those meanings is a semantic change at the owning artifact's gate,
not a schema cleanup. OpenSpec artifacts remain outside this migration authority.

# Generator request security and audit — candidate

Proposed behavior for REQ-polaris-generation-021/022. This document grants no
credential, consent, exposure change or operational effect. Existing RFC5
mechanism choices and effective owner acts remain controlling.

## Authenticate the caller, then authorize the operation

Every authenticated act names exactly one principal: owner, machine client or
Syzygy acting through its adapter. Authorization uses that principal's explicit
scopes and project access, never the assumption that one human owns everything.
Audit/consent/approval records name their principal. A successful login is not
permission to start a run, read another project, export or adopt a draft.

Requests have only the existing two client classes. A valid machine credential
classifies the request as machine; other requests must satisfy browser discipline.
Network location, first-party packaging and absent Origin headers classify no
identity. Official CLI/protocol clients use their own machine credentials;
session cookies are not transferable machine credentials. A browser presenting
a machine credential does not obtain a browser session.

The route inventory covers project/source selection, request preparation,
start/resume/retry, progress and artifact retrieval, cancellation/rejection,
profile/consent/approval ceremonies, authorship, reversal, export and recovery.
Each route declares whether it serves project data or changes state, required
principal scopes, project/subject resolution, and the effective gates it invokes.
Changing an identifier in a request never changes what the caller may access.

## Browser and machine admission

Data-bearing and state-changing browser routes require an owner-attended session,
including on loopback. Sessions have declared maximum lifetime and immediate
owner revocation effective at the next request. Without a declared lifetime they
do not persist beyond the process. Session identity is credential-based, not
device/IP-based. Reauthentication restores admission, not revoked project consent.

Every state-changing browser request requires per-session anti-forgery proof.
Present Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site values must satisfy the active allowlist;
absent headers neither admit nor condemn, and the proof still applies. Host must
belong to the exposure mode's closed hostname set before application logic.
Origin matching alone is not a session or anti-forgery proof.

Machine credentials identify one opaque machine client, are explicitly scoped,
and are issued only through the existing owner-attended ceremony. An unscoped
credential is invalid. Rotation preserves client identity and uses only the
owner-declared overlap; revocation can target identity or instance and applies
at the next request. The server stores only a verifier, not a presentable secret.
Credential governance metadata contains identity, scopes, issuance/expiry and
revocation, never secret bytes. Neither another machine credential nor observed
project content can issue one.

Unauthenticated access is limited to health/liveness and authentication bootstrap,
without project data; the existing interface-qualified device restrictions and
owner-attended issuance still apply. Fresh installation stays loopback-only.
Any non-loopback serving requires the effective exposure act, declared hosts,
TLS and owner-device restriction, plus full application authentication. Overlay
device identity is not client identity. This feature enables no new exposure mode.

## Keep request, execution and adapter identities distinct

A background run uses its independently valid execution warrant and Syzygy's
authorized adapter credentials. Expiry of the initiating browser session blocks
subsequent requests from that session; it does not retroactively revoke a valid
execution warrant. A worker cannot continue using the expired session as its own
credential. Each later effect still checks current consent/profile/adapter scope.

Adapter credentials are a separate, per-adapter/per-authority population, scoped
to the permitted effects, never indexed or surfaced. They and credentials that
authenticate to Syzygy are never injectable into observed-project execution.
Adapter effects are attributed to Syzygy, with initiating request provenance
linked separately rather than pretending the owner's browser performed them.

## Revocation changes enforcement immediately

Request admission, provider egress and artifact writes check current credential,
consent and applicable profile state at the attempted act. An earlier scheduler
observation, dispatch reservation or authored-write commitment is no exemption.
Already transmitted work may be in flight; revocation does not prove remote
termination or erase incurred charges. Supported cancellation, uncertain effects
and late receipts retain their real outcomes. Observed-code execution, if ever
separately authorized, retains its own stricter profile termination obligations.

Recording revocation immediately labels every subsequently served dependent
claim with withdrawal and triggers a new identified evaluation. Until it
completes, the previous evaluated value remains with the withdrawal visible;
the security act does not rewrite immutable claim values itself. The owner can
see what was revoked, when, by whom and the resulting dependent states. Restoring
permission requires a fresh grant/record, not silently flipping a revoked flag.

## Protected audit trail

Each admission, denial, egress, run launch, adapter effect, consent grant or
revocation, and credential issuance/rotation/revocation emits an audit record.
It carries principal, credential or session identity, act, subject, exposure
mode, actual act instant and outcome, plus durable evidence identity, integrity,
source, capture time, scope and provenance. An unresolved identity on a refused
request is explicit; the recorder never fabricates an owner principal or logs a
presented credential to fill the field. Act instant, capture time and claim
evaluation/as-of time remain distinct.

The trail resides outside the governed plane and outside the untrusted actor
class's write reach. A work record, file in the repository, or owner-user-only
directory writable by the same untrusted process is not that boundary. The
chosen recorder/storage must demonstrate protection against those writers.
Audit records contain no credential values, secrets or excluded bodies; rejected
offending payloads use permitted digest provenance, never payload values.
An unverifiable audit correlation cannot make an owner-act record effective.

The proposed outage behavior is a design choice, not an atomicity claim in
RFC5-25: before a new spending, content-release, generation/adoption or artifact
write effect, the recorder must durably accept its identified admission/attempt
record. If it cannot, refuse that new effect with audit availability explicitly
unresolved. Do not claim the failed audit write was recorded.

Audit outage does not delay an authenticated, authorized local run stop,
cancellation of an existing attempt through its permitted control route, or denial
of further use of the identity/permission named by a valid revocation request.
These specific stop controls still require current caller authority; the exception
permits no new generation, export, content release, artifact reversal/deletion or
permission grant. Local cancellation retains its ordering against dispatch and
write commitment; remote cancellation is only attempted where permitted and its
outcome is never presumed.

Apply the protective hold immediately and retain permitted pending-event metadata
through the trusted recorder/recovery boundary. If required durable audit or
owner-act correlation cannot be established, show enforcement held with formal
revocation/audit pending, not a successfully verified revocation or an invented
fallback authority state. The hold cannot silently clear on service recovery;
resolve it through the governing revocation/grant mechanism with trustworthy
records. Missing pending-event durability stays Unknown and cannot be reconstructed
as trusted ceremony evidence from a mutable work file. Once revocation is validly
recorded, its ordinary withdrawal-label and forced-evaluation rules apply. A pending attempt proves only admission/intent to attempt, not
provider transmission, run success or a completed write.

After the effect, append the actual outcome linked to that identity. A lost
outcome acknowledgment does not prove no effect and never permits blind replay.
Recover from authoritative receipts under current permission and append the
missing outcome idempotently; unavailable evidence stays uncertain. Existing
protected records remain immutable. This protocol does not promise a transaction
spanning the audit store and an external provider or rollback of an incurred
effect. Audit-dependent confirmation remains unmet while required evidence is
missing. Exact durable recorder/transport behavior needs implementation testing.

## Existing-host integration evidence

[Observed] In this worktree, the POC browser-origin helper checks host/origin, and
the credential helper persists a presentable token used for comparison. Those
inspected behaviors alone do not establish session/anti-forgery admission,
per-client scopes and rotation, verifier-only server storage or protected audit.
Relevant source: `apps/three-surface-poc/src/browser-origin.ts` and
`packages/cap1-daemon/src/credentials.ts`. No credential store was read.

Reuse the existing host mechanisms where their contracts and behavior match;
repair or extend the remaining integration explicitly. Required changes to
existing capability behavior must appear in the overlap/impact review before
sign-off. This document does not treat current route labels or passing read-only
admission tests as proof for the new mutating operations.

## Proposed implementation binding

EFFECT-HOST-DESIGN.md specifies the local origin/process isolation, protected
recorder principals and append/query/recovery interfaces for this candidate.
It also names the excluded-actor and restart/outage tests. Its deployment must
prove those boundaries before real effects; ordinary same-user files or test
adapters cannot stand in for the protected recorder.

# Source admission, classification and exclusions — candidate

Proposed detail for REQ-polaris-generation-025, supplementing existing admission,
adapter, audit and revocation requirements. It grants no new read, write, provider
or execution consent and changes no adopted project's screening policy.

## Resolve the actual authority and consent records

The observing project and its governance root come from the owning declarations;
they are not inferred from the generated page's label or an observed repository's
directory. Observation/write consent is per repository. Egress consent is one
record per project/provider pair naming permitted content classes. Execution
consent is per project for an exact approved execution-profile version. Each
record grants exactly one consent class and records its subject, scope, granting
principal, grant instant and revocation state. Those classes remain separately
revocable and visible; permission to read never implies permission to send,
write or run observed code.

Adapter registration, classification-policy approval, secret-policy approval and
consent are separate authority checks. A genuine consent record does not make an
unapproved permissive policy effective. A policy's approval warrants its use,
not the truth of a generated claim or success of a transmission or screening.

## Carry content provenance through composition

The egress vocabulary remains governance-text, code-structure, code-content,
work-history, evidence-content and derived-composites. The effective declared
classification policy classifies concrete content and determines the composite's
inherited highest embedded class from its actual input provenance. Composing a
prompt, summary or embedding carries embedded classifications and origins forward;
the composer's self-assigned output label cannot replace that derivation.

No total order is invented from the vocabulary's printed or lexical order, and
this contract does not introduce a separate requirement that every embedded
class appear independently in consent. The approved policy must make the
inherited classification determinable. Where its rules or input provenance do
not determine it, refuse egress and show the refusal. Derived-composites consent
alone never launders otherwise unconsented content. Classification results and
policy versions stay auditable and identity-bound to the snapshot.

Every network transmission of governed-project content crosses the single egress
check, including side effects and remote backing dependencies. At the actual
effect boundary it verifies the in-force project/provider consent, determinable
permitted classification under an effectively adopted policy, and the consent's
own effective act. Both acts' exact provenance states are disclosed. An invalid
purported consent act refuses transmission and produces the prescribed
Contradiction; mere absence is not fabricated into a purported act. None of these
checks can be supplied by a provider response or registration label.

## Screen at every ingest, under the observer's policy

Before content enters any store, surface or endpoint, apply the observing
project's effectively approved secret-detection policy bound to its exact digest.
This includes source acquisition, cross-project reads, workspace imports,
provider responses, evidence, adapter results, telemetry and diagnostic metadata;
the examples are not an exemption list. The observed project's policy text is
data to screen, not authority to replace the observer's policy.

The policy version is a snapshot input and its exact act provenance is visible.
Missing or invalid policy authority blocks ingestion. Secret matches and content
that cannot be classified are excluded, not indexed pending a later review.
Approval of the detector is never displayed as proof that the content contains
no secrets. No content field or newly introduced route bypasses the boundary.

## Preserve useful surviving evidence

Exclusion provenance records content digest, location reference, policy version
and one of the existing redaction classes. Excluded bytes never enter the record,
audit or any other store. Location metadata is also subject to screening; an
opaque permitted reference can locate an exclusion without exposing an excluded
path string.

| Redaction class | Observable result |
|---|---|
| excluded-artifact | Withhold the artifact; every dependent claim is Unknown with excluded-content and the exclusion count. |
| unclassifiable-excluded | Withhold the unclassifiable artifact under the same Unknown/count rule; this is the fail-closed default. |
| redacted-span | Retain permitted surviving content and counted markers. Claims supported by surviving content keep their otherwise-earned tier and disclose the redaction count; only claims depending on removed spans become Unknown with excluded-content. |

This table defines branch semantics, not permission to choose a more permissive
branch. If an adopted project policy permits only whole-artifact exclusion, the
generator cannot introduce partial redaction. Its source/claim support mapping
must be sufficient to distinguish surviving support from removed support; missing
classification/support information cannot be repaired by guessing.

## Revocation does not rewrite challenge history

The immediate enforcement, withdrawal label and forced evaluation in REQ-022
remain the common mechanism. A revoked provider's overlays are not recomputed
and admit no new kernel challenges. Already-admitted challenges keep their
lifecycle and leave only through their governing resolution act; revocation
neither silently resolves nor unsuspends them. Historical records remain with
withdrawal visible. This concerns the kernel Challenge lifecycle, not a ban on
the owner reporting a problem or drafting a repair.

Existing Butlers admission and screening rules remain controlling. A new generic
schema, an available source file or a useful README finding cannot broaden its
consented population or relax its literal grammar. Any needed policy/registry
change is a separately reviewed and authorized change, not generator fallback.

# Generation progress and work state — candidate

Proposed detail for REQ-polaris-generation-028. It adopts no mapping or bound,
does not extend a closed vocabulary, and does not activate deferred fleet control.

## Show actual progress in its own field

Generation can report recorded facts such as request admitted, response captured,
draft persisted or review completed. Those are stage/receipt facts, not normalized
work states or proof that a worker is currently alive. A stale last-recorded stage
is identified as such; the UI cannot turn an old dispatch claim into a live
progress signal. Local cancellation remains the separately specified operation.

The normalized work value is derived per evaluation, not stored as editable
scheduler state or minted as a Claim. It uses the exact thirteen-value vocabulary:
future, planned, ready, active, blocked, review, merged, reconciled,
closed-unmerged, state-undetermined, eligibility-undetermined,
activity-undetermined and stale-or-dead. Raw substrate state remains qualified,
visible and queryable beside it, read from the tool's declared vocabulary rather
than a hardcoded client list. The effective, versioned normalization declaration
is a snapshot input under RFC2-1 item 7; a self-declared mapping grants no authority.

Each rendering, filter, count, export and machine answer carries separately
qualified normalized and chain fields, including normalized reconciled. The chain
keeps its existing six values. Normalized reconciled requires the underlying
reconciled@E verdict's tier and evaluation identity; it has no independent Claim
identity or observation-record membership. Missing verdict support cannot become
a positive state. State-local absence values never become claim Unknown reasons.

## Derive only from the named evaluation

Ready derives from that evaluation's captured work export and dependency feed,
not a live scheduler readiness command. New dispatch admission captures fresh
inputs into its own identified evaluation; it cannot change an older displayed
ready answer or reuse that answer as current effect authority.

The existing state predicates remain controlling:

- Future is approved/queued execution intent before materialization, with its
  sub-state and order. Unapproved drafts remain unadopted, and incompatible
  alternatives cannot be summed as parallel remaining work.
- Planned distinguishes deliberate freezing from unmet dependencies; missing
  eligibility inputs yield eligibility-undetermined with the missing input shown.
- Active requires claimed work and a permitted progress signal within an
  effectively declared bound. Review describes an exact-head review lane, not
  reviewer liveness.
- Blocked carries every derived cause from dependency, pr-wait, external and
  decision. Cause-Unknown appears only when no cause derives, never mixed into a
  nonempty set. Counts/filters/answers retain the set.
- Merged requires VCS merge evidence. Closure without it is closed-unmerged with
  the native reason or its explicit absence; neither is done or satisfied intent.
  Reconciliation remains separate, with absent V0 computation honestly Unknown.
- Unmapped native values remain state-undetermined with raw value and mapping
  route. Missing bounds and expired signals retain their specified absence cases;
  the generator does not widen those predicates itself.

Worker liveness uses only the qualifying branch-tip/commit/PR progress signals
under RFC4-23, with their actual instant and effective bound. Provider responses,
draft saves, coordinator heartbeats, locks and worktree presence are not substitute
signals. Between signals liveness is Unknown; an old signal shows stale-or-dead
and its real instant. Missing/ineffective bounds cannot make active renderable.

### Exact phase and consumer applicability
